_readme: Recordings whose sung work has been IDENTIFIED and then verified absent from data/composition_registry.json. Keyed by the recording's path relative to the repo root. scripts/parse_negative_labels.py promotes an item to the 'ooc' stratum only if its source path appears here; everything else that carries sung words but resolves to nothing is 'sung_unidentified', which is reported and never gates.
_schema: <relative audio path>: {work, evidence, checked_exact, checked_relaxed, reviewed_by, reviewed_on}. 'work' is the actual composition being sung, in whatever transliteration the source gives. 'evidence' must say how the identity was established -- liner notes, an announcement in the audio, a trustworthy archive field -- because a filename that fails to resolve is candidate generation, not truth (CODEX_NEGATIVE_ARM_REVIEW.md section 2).
_status_2026_07_28: EMPTY, and this is a finding rather than an omission. Of 1238 recordings in data/concert_audio, 1175 resolve exactly, 16 resolve under the relaxed key, 36 are free-form sections, and the remaining 11 have no work identity at all: they are upload ids ('1224830 aswinsainarain'), shellac catalogue numbers ('HMV P 5866 G C -8-10152'), archive slot names ('Concert 163', 'xxxx'), or a genre plus a raga with no title ('varnam vasantha'). None of them names a composition, so none can be verified absent from the catalog. The corpus is a Carnatic-composition corpus whose registry was partly built from these very filenames, so it cannot supply out-of-catalog truth. Measuring OOC abstention at 300s needs prospectively acquired audio with trustworthy titles -- pending Deepti.
